newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: HAVEL HAILS CLINTON MOVES TOWARDS EAST EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: HAVEL HAILS CLINTON MOVES TOWARDS EAST EUROPE.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel hailed President Bill Clinton on Wednesday, saying he had promoted U.S. relations with post-communist Europe and security in the entire north Atlantic region.
Havel, a firm supporter of Czech membership of NATO, made the comments in a statement after sending Clinton a telegram congratulating him on his re-election.

"Already in his previous term of office President Clinton has in many cases contributed to a deepening of political and economic relations of his country with the states of central and eastern Europe and set out to build the basis for new stability in the whole Euro-Atlantic region," said the statement issued by Havel's office.
Last month Clinton pleased the Czech Republic and other former East Bloc countries by calling for the NATO defence alliance to recruit the first batch of former Soviet satellites by 1999.
The Czechs, along with Poland, Hungary and Slovenia, are tipped as frontrunners for early membership.
Havel acknowledged the U.S. role in international security.

"The president of the United States carries, as the representative of one of the world powers, responsibility not only for the security, freedom and happiness of American citizens, but also an important influence on the protection of peace and security in the entire world," the statement said.
The Czech Foreign Ministry stressed Clinton's plan for expanding NATO within three years.

"The continuing active role of the United States on the European continent and the commitment of President Clinton that the North Atlantic Alliance is to be expanded in the year 1999 is an important signal for stability in Europe," it said in a statement.
